The specification-driven calculations reproduce the retained B1 and A3 endpoints and the declared B1 phase-state subset in [issue #228](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/228). These are numerical reproduction checks against the #222 calculations. They establish neither new physical validation nor qualification for absorber use. Delivered evidence awaits independent review and investigator promotion.

The shared [TOML declarations](declarations.toml) own species supports, reactions and their temperature-domain amendment, the neutral reference, seven named problem templates, observation constructors, row column maps, roles, residual scales and weights. [B1](B1.toml) and [A3](A3.toml) bind parameter, coordinate and caloric records by SHA-256. The driver expands prepared CSV rows at execution time. Preparation performs fixed source transformations; it defines no chemistry or observation constructor and imports no historical script. The generated per-row problem document was removed.

The 280 fitted observations retain eight groups: 69 Kuranov, 16 Jakobsen, 40 Carson, four Merkley, 33 heat capacities, 33 loaded densities, 24 unloaded densities and 61 Kim pressures. Their order, source rows, fixed transformations and residual definitions remain explicit. R1 and R5 use the retained endpoints. R2 uses the retained B1 start with the declared zero MDEAH⁺–water reciprocal-temperature slope, original coordinate origins, scales, bounds and target ties. The controls remain 40 maximum iterations, 2100 s maximum elapsed time, function and parameter tolerances 1e-10, and gradient tolerance 1e-8. The native termination is function tolerance reached: relative cost change 3.932338e-12 ≤1e-10. Native rank is nine; active bounds are coordinate indices 5 and 8 (zero-based). Covariance remains marked `active_bound`; it is not unrestricted parameter uncertainty.

R4 includes the 745 fitted and comparison states and six formal Merkley cap states. The endpoint-bound [phase input table](inputs/phase-states.csv) preserves distinct observation identities, including physically repeated states. [Phase provenance](inputs/phase-provenance.json) binds the source files and selected loadings to B1 endpoint hash `1d0d80832f282cde85acab294501ca9ec8dbc34cddf8edf2eebf6e1e1d03949d`. An initial mapping used source caps for four fitted Merkley endpoint states, producing three additional gas witnesses; comparison with the retained native state amounts identified the input error. Using the retained selected loadings restored the exact 37 identities without changing search controls or classification. The classifier decodes Engine's returned logarithmic packing fraction, with threshold 0.10 and open ambiguity interval (0.05, 0.35). The nine supplemental states from local saturation inversion are excluded. This endpoint check supplies no automatic phase coverage for another fit.

[Complete phase trials](results/R4-trials.json.gz), [phase counts and identities](results/R4.json), [native fit diagnostics](results/R2.json) and [endpoint residual evidence](results/endpoint-checks.json) retain the numerical evidence. Phase trials larger than 5 MB are gzip-compressed. The standalone environment uses the merged Engine commit `d513820994a78bfe628d42fffd55b2eeab6f89bd` and wheel SHA-256 `ca7093ca721fdc80226c74d018a582f31705684c6995e80b0492c193334dd5d5`; installed Engine files are byte-identical to the wheel. [Runtime evidence](results/runtime.json) records Python 3.13.14, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, 32 workers and one BLAS thread per worker. Root dependency pins are unchanged.

The [comparison records](results/comparisons.json) retain all 432 requested comparisons: 406 available, 25 outside the declared 293.15–395 K assessment interval, and one native `CentralSolveUnavailable`. The 333.15 K, 60 wt% formal Merkley state has diagnostic loading 0.8069104066798605 mol CO₂/mol MDEA but no native capped-heat endpoint loading. Its native refusal remains unavailable despite its formal phase check. The Ermatchkov statistic is conditional outside-fit pressure assessment. Finite search coverage, accepted active bounds, unmodeled nitrogen headspace and property-specific extrapolation or unavailability remain limitations. Reproduction tolerances describe numerical agreement and do not represent experimental uncertainty.

The [partial handoff](results/handoff.json) contains chemistry, named species/phase/feed declarations, calorics, runtime identity and assessment references with hashes. The fitted parameter document remains explicitly unavailable under the accepted export-scope revision and [Engine #928](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/928). The missing declaration is a public serializer from the native `ParameterDocument` returned by `reg.fitted_parameters` / `_core.fitted_document` to the `epcsaft.parameters` JSON form read by `Parameters.from_json`. No local parameter-document updater or ASL column handoff was added. The required future check exports the B1 refit, reloads it and reproduces its cost within 1e-8 relative.

The local literature shelf was absent. This work uses the accepted retained numerical references and does not claim a fresh paper audit. The notebook is not registered through the manuscript management command because the owner excluded edits to `analyses/_cse-manuscript.json`.

Delivery-review corrections retain the same numerical scope. The MDEA ideal-gas heat capacity is the retained Neumann-primary cubic, recentered at 313.15 K: $C_p=\sum_k a_k(T-313.15\,\mathrm K)^k$. Native evaluation at the anchor gives 198.77937643331074 J/(mol K). The prior uncentered Wangler label was incorrect; coefficient values are unchanged. The handoff hashes the parameter and caloric preparation provenance.

Coordinate declarations now dispatch `kind = "reaction_coordinate"` and `kind = "reaction_enthalpy_shift"` to the respective native constructors, with `name`, origin, scale and bounds, plus coefficient or pivot temperature. The check follows Engine commit d513820, `engine/docs/equations.md`, `reaction_constant_coordinate_derivative`, and the `Coordinate` and `reg.reaction_coordinate` docstrings: $q=\mathrm{origin}+\mathrm{scale}\,v$ assigns a stored coefficient of natural $\ln K$. For a source enthalpy increment $h$, $\delta a=h/(RT_p)$ and $\delta b=-h/R$, preserving $\ln K$ at $T_p$. The production path uses the Engine constructor, native physical coefficient rows (`EvaluatedCoordinates.physical`, after the EOS and held-diameter rows) and completed native enthalpy-shift laws (`reaction_laws`); the direct formula appears only in the numerical comparison.

On retained Kuranov row `fit:11` at 333.13 K, the objective at zero optimizer value is 0.1264081715573054. Assigning $a=a_0+0.2$ gives cost 0.5571628213373777 versus direct-law cost 0.5571628213373779. A 1000 J/mol shift about 313.15 K gives cost 0.1603266808251767 versus 0.16032668082517665 from the directly modified law. Both zero optimizer values reproduce the unshifted pressure 162212.48927863713 Pa. The largest cost difference is 2.22e-16, below the 1e-10 numerical-equivalence tolerance. [Coefficient evidence](results/reaction_coordinate-check.json) and [enthalpy-shift evidence](results/reaction_enthalpy_shift-check.json) retain both zero and nonzero cases. Fitted reaction declarations from those native chart outputs are now retained in the fit report and consumed by the handoff.

The missing/nonfinite split-coordinate check now precedes exponentiation. A focused failure-injection assertion retains a −∞ trial as one unresolved record with its cause and zero gas-evolution classifications. This assertion tests failure reporting; it is not a physical phase observation. The prior R4 trials contain no such nonfinite coordinate and remain the independently confirmed reproduction evidence.
